items.title: ‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine Yamal

items.title: Watching Cavan Sullivan, excitement is tempered by memories of hypetrains past
items.summary: The 16-year-old Union star isn’t the first wunderkind to be feted by the American soccersphere The trouble with trying not to hype up Cavan Sullivan is that he keeps on doing cool stuff. Like this past weekend, when he scampers along on a Philadelphia Union breakaway, loses his man by stopping so suddenly it’s as if he’s pulled a ripcord, back-heels the cutback behind his standing leg, watches it slowly kiss off the far post and in, and celebrated the goal by bowing and doffing an imaginary top hat to the crowd. Like when he doubles the score by setting up an attack and finishing it himself with a left-footed lash through the goalkeeper’s legs form an acute angle.

items.title: Craig Bellamy says his loyalty to Wales is unquestionable after rejecting Burnley
items.summary: Staying with Wales over Burnley a ‘simple choice’ Never claiming expenses cited as a show of commitment Craig Bellamy said Wales supporters should never question his commitment to the cause after he rejected the chance to manage Burnley, pointing to how he got solicitors’ letters to play for his country and refused to claim expenses on international duty. Bellamy held talks with Burnley in the summer after the Championship club triggered a release clause in his contract but turned down the move because Wales was “the right place for me”.

items.title: Oscar Bobb takes Fulham past stubborn West Ham and into Carabao Cup last 16
items.summary: Álvaro Arbeloa played in some great defences but whether he knows how to coach one remains to be seen. ­Fulham have been fragile since appointing the Spaniard and they were fortunate not to be dragged into a penalty shootout by West Ham as this entertainingCarabao Cup tie drew to a close. West Ham equalised twice during the first half and they almost did it again after Oscar Bobb made it 3-2 in the 78th minute.

items.title: Raheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxide
items.summary: Ex-England footballer pleads guilty and admits to failing to provide a specimen as he appears in court Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and could be sent to prison after driving his ­Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide. The former Chelsea and Manchester City forward stood in the dock to accept three charges before ­ Basingstoke magistrates court heard how he embarked on a ­prolonged period of reckless driving on the M25 and M3, inhaling nitrous oxide ­balloons, before crashing his £270,000 car. Sterling was disqualified from driving and bailed until 25 November, when his sentence will either be determined or referred to the crown court.

items.title: In Manchester, Premier League superiority is now separated by Haaland’s cutting edge
items.summary: In a bad-tempered meeting at Old Trafford, United and City showed they are far from the finished product Sign up for our free newsletter here While London has a host of top-flight clubs and Liverpool have been regular contenders, the story of the Premier League can almost entirely be told with Mancunian main characters. From Manchester United’s decade-plus of dominance under Sir Alex Ferguson to Manchester City’s emergence among the oil baron class, with a grip made firmer under Pep Guardiola’s guidance, it seems one must always beat a Manchester club to the title. Never before has the trophy spent more three seasons before returning to one of these two clubs, with a pair of three-year roadshows in the mid-2000s and mid-2010s.

items.title: Enzo Fernández’s fortitude shows Maresca was right to crave City reunion | Will Unwin
items.summary: Some scoffed at £125m price tag, but the Argentinian did the work of two midfielders after Phil Foden’s red card Enzo Maresca does not pay the bills at Manchester City but he is ecstatic that those who do spent £125m for him to be reunited with Enzo Fernández. The manager and the midfielder were together at Chelsea, forming a strong bond over a relatively short time, one the Italian knew could provide the final piece within his master plan. The Argentinian was equally eager to work under Maresca once more and made it abundantly clear to his previous employers where he saw his future.

items.title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League Cup
items.summary: Derek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but the Rangers manager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season. Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease.

items.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
items.summary: The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge. Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half.
